issues.description: The problem statement specifies a function named _detect_errors(...) (leading underscore) while the template and reference solution provide and expect a function named detect_errors(...) (no leading underscore). This name mismatch is a structural inconsistency: students reading the problem may implement or search for _detect_errors but the provided template/tests reference detect_errors, causing confusion or failing lookups.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to refer to detect_errors(...) (no leading underscore), or (B) rename the template/solution function to _detect_errors(...) to match the problem text. Ensure the tests (if any) reference the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement names the error-detection function _detect_errors (leading underscore) while both the template and the solution implement and document detect_errors (no underscore). This mismatch can confuse students about which function to implement and which symbol the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the name consistent across artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to refer to detect_errors (remove the leading underscore), or alternatively rename the function in msd.py to _detect_errors and provide the same name in the solution. Prefer changing the problem statement to detect_errors so it matches the template and solution.
